findings.claim: The overlap treats normalized continuous sections as a theorem to relocate and optionally prove again in ProfiniteCohomology Layer 0. The exact general theorem, including normalization and the between-quotients version, already exists at the mandated Tau Ceti pin. The finite-kernel case is a specialization, so the actionable rescope proposal should identify a library import instead of moving a proof obligation between upstream roadmaps.
findings.evidence: The proposal says "Remove the finite-kernel section milestone" and offers to move its elementary proof into PC Layer 0. Reviewed AUDIT-22 coverage for PPG Layer 5 classifies this target tauceti. Read https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369/TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/Group/Profinite/Section.lean#L226: TauCeti.exists_continuous_section assumes a compact totally disconnected topological group and IsClosed H, and returns a continuous right inverse s with s(mk 1)=1. Lines 253–258 give exists_continuous_section_of_le for K≤H, normalized at the identity. Finite normal N is closed, satisfying the first declaration directly. Both statements and their proofs were read at the pin on 2026-09-30.
findings.fix: Rewrite this overlap as reuse of TauCeti.exists_continuous_section and exists_continuous_section_of_le, with finite-kernel specialization and any genuinely needed wrapper/comparison only. Preserve the upstream roadmap identities. Do not create a new section-theorem task or request that an already formalized proof be moved/reproved. Record the pinned names and the reviewed audit classification in the overlap and examined entry.

findings.where: research/blueprint/links/tauceti_TauCetiRoadmap_ProfiniteProPGroups.json; links[11] (PC10 → PPG6), together with links[32] and the cited PC10 contract
findings.claim: The all-degree supplier is correctly needed, but its advertised Shapiro construction requires an impossible chain isomorphism between the two canonical homogeneous-cochain complexes. The link map imports that supplier without flagging the false construction. Shapiro is a cohomology isomorphism; for these specific complexes it must be supplied by a quasi-isomorphism or a chain-homotopy equivalence, not an isomorphism in each degree.
findings.evidence: content/tau-ceti/ProfiniteCohomology/README.md, Layer 10, says "Construct a chain isomorphism" named shapiroCochainIso between the canonical complexes. The accepted link PC10→PPG6 explicitly imports all-degree shapiroIso, acyclicity and dimensionShiftIso. Read https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174/Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/Basic.lean#L94 through L131: resolution'X X n=resolutionX X (n+1), and homogeneousCochains takes invariants of that shifted resolution. For finite G=C2, closed H=1 and A=F2, C^0(G,Coind_1^G A) is (canonically) the coefficient module Coind_1^G A=Map(C2,F2), of dimension 2, while C^0(1,A)=F2 has dimension 1. In homogeneous notation the first term consists of equivariant maps C2→Map(C2,F2), again determined by one arbitrary vector. An exhaustive diagnostic counted four versus two elements. Thus no degree-zero isomorphism, and hence no chain isomorphism, exists. The usual Shapiro cohomology statement remains valid.
findings.fix: Retain the PC10→PPG6 dependency, and the all-degree exactness dependency PC10→PPG7. Add the precise supplier correction/maintainer request to the link packet: replace shapiroCochainIso by a named chain comparison with a quasi-isomorphism proof (or explicit homotopy inverse), deriving shapiroIso on cohomology and proving low-degree compatibility. Keep dimension shifting and coinduced acyclicity downstream of this corrected interface. Do not invent a PPG-local Shapiro theory or silently weaken the consumer result.

findings.where: research/blueprint/links/tauceti_TauCetiRoadmap_ProfiniteProPGroups.json; missing PPG Layer 4 → ProfiniteCohomology example links; examined ProfiniteCohomology
findings.claim: The map records only incoming ProfiniteCohomology links and misses its explicit need for the owned profinite-integer group in the examples of PC Layers 4, 6, 10 and 11. The omission leaves a second construction or an invalid weakening: the consumer permits an arbitrary procyclic group with a generator, which is insufficient for the stated cohomology formulas. A cyclic finite group is already a counterexample.
findings.evidence: PPG opening ownership boundary says "zHat as a profinite *group* (Layer 4)" and Layer 4 supplies the rank-one completion interface; this is also the supplier used in links 19–21. content/tau-ceti/ProfiniteCohomology/README.md §6, lines 1731–1736, assigns its example to Layers 4,6,10,11 and says "Build Ẑ as the profinite completion of ℤ", or use "an arbitrary procyclic group". The example asserts H²(Ẑ,M)=0 for torsion M and cd_p Ẑ=1. PC11 repeats these as First values. Take G=C2 with its generator and trivial M=F2: the normalized cocycle c(1,1)=1, c(0,a)=c(a,0)=0 is nonzero in H². Every normalized coboundary has value 0 at (1,1), so H²(C2,F2)=F2. Exhaustive bar enumeration found two normalized cocycles and one coboundary. Thus the permitted arbitrary-procyclic replacement is false, even though the Ẑ theorem is true. No such outgoing edge occurs in any of the 25 accepted link packets checked.
findings.fix: Add evidence-backed links from PPG Layer 4 to the actual example stages PC4, PC6, PC10 and PC11, using the source ownership statement and each stage/§6 reference. Specify reuse of zHat with its completion universal property, or an explicit isomorphism to that exact group, rather than generic procyclicity. Record a supplier-document correction for the maintainer removing the arbitrary-procyclic alternative. Keep the cohomology proof in ProfiniteCohomology and the profinite group carrier in its existing owner; this requires no new ring-of-profinite-integers task.
